mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 persons for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in more than 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency monetary easing that boosts risk appetite and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of emergency rate-cut episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and real personal savings (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month +5% AND RSAFS > previous month +5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for five consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and higher corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.5% for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in more than 60% of triggered periods.
